headline: Amina carries 70.48 adjusted share and Farah carries 48.33, a gap of 22 points against a circle mean of 62.67.
what_i_tried: Moved overnight stays from Amina to Rian because distance weighting made them lighter for Rian
Shifted Friday medication tasks from Amina to Rian to consolidate weekend responsibility
Attempted to move work from Amina to Farah but every task Amina holds either falls on Friday or Saturday when Farah is unavailable or involves night shifts which Farah refuses
Tried all four legal task moves from Amina to Rian across four rounds but each attempt widened the gap between Rian and Farah more than it narrowed the gap between Amina and Farah
the_tension: Farah holds fifteen tasks but her adjusted share is lowest because distance makes her work less costly. Amina and Rian live closer or must travel for in-person tasks, so their hours carry more weight. Every task Amina holds that might balance the load falls on days Farah stated she is unavailable or requires night shifts Farah stated she refuses. Moving work from Amina to Rian narrows one gap but widens another. The stated availability and refusal limits do not permit a split that satisfies proportionality within tolerance.

options.label: Keep the current split
options.consequence: All three siblings accepted their shares. Amina carries more than proportional weight by 22 adjusted points. The tasks respect every stated limit.

options.label: Ask Farah to expand availability to Friday or Saturday or to accept night shifts
options.consequence: This would open moves that can shift burden from Amina to Farah directly. It requires Farah to change a stated boundary.

options.label: Ask Amina to release one or more of her stated limits so that her current tasks can be reassigned
options.consequence: This might create legal moves that reduce her adjusted share. It requires Amina to change a stated boundary.

what_i_will_not_decide: I will not choose between these options because I do not know what any of you are carrying outside this schedule or why your limits are where they are. One of you may be shouldering something I cannot see. Deciding whose boundary should bend is a family question, not a scheduling question.
